title: Wendell and the Cover
premise: Beatrix Coldharbour, a whistle-blower living under four names, receives a call on a burner phone she buried two decades ago — the voice belongs to her presumed-dead handler, warning that the dossier she once leaked is being weaponized by the very agency she exposed. Hunted by an assassin who knows all four of her names, she must smuggle the original evidence across three jurisdictions before a treaty signing buries it forever. In the end, she trades her anonymity for the truth, publishing the dossier as the assassin corners her — and discovers the voice on the phone was her own, recorded years ago by the handler as a failsafe, meaning the past has been guiding her home all along.
about_author: Wendell Coldharbour is the pen name of a former intelligence archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing documents that officially never existed. This is a debut thriller drawn from a single file that went missing from the archive — and from the author's own memory.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Living quietly as 'Margaret Voss' in a coastal town, Beatrix answers a burner phone she buried twenty years ago; the voice of her dead handler warns her the dossier is resurfacing. That night, someone burns down the house of her third identity. Emotional beat: dread and the vertigo of a past that refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Grave
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix, with an intercut chapter from the assassin 'Corvus', who methodically eliminates her aliases. Beatrix digs up the handler's grave and finds it empty except for a case containing the original dossier and a second phone. Emotional beat: grief curdling into resolve as loyalty to the dead handler collides with the truth he hid from her.

chapters.title: Three Borders, One Assassin
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix and Corvus in alternating chapters. A cross-border race to reach a journalist before the treaty signing; Corvus corners her in a freight yard, and instead of killing her, reveals the agency ordered him to erase the handler's trail — and that Beatrix is the last name on his list. Emotional beat: betrayal, then an uneasy, transactional alliance.

chapters.title: The Cover
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. At the signing, she broadcasts the dossier while Corvus holds off the agency's cleaners; the failsafe recording plays — her own voice, left by the handler — revealing the handler staged his death to protect her. She surrenders to the press, not the governments, and finally belongs to her real name. Emotional beat: costly, hard-won peace.
